panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient's skin lesion on the left back. The article title identifies the lesion as arising from Penicillium marneffei (Talaromyces marneffei) infection in an AIDS patient, and the in-text description (3 × 3 cm, flesh-colored, well-demarcated, ulcerated lesion; skin biopsy culture positive for P. marneffei) confirms talaromycosis. The lesion is a raised papule/plaque with central depression and hemorrhagic-necrotic crust, consistent with a papulonecrotic-type cutaneous talaromycosis lesion; the article labels it an unusual appearing lesion, so it is classified as a variant rather than classic. Skin appears light; no ethnicity, age, or stage is stated.
